item.title: Canva Adds AI Off Button and Library Content Controls
item.description:
Canva Adds AI Off Button and Library Content Controls

Canva has introduced a new toggle that allows users to turn off its generative AI features. This update responds to user requests for control over the platform’s expanding array of AI-powered tools.

🔍 Overview

The new feature provides a way to disable Canva’s generative AI capabilities, including its chatbot for image generation and specific editing tools. Users can also adjust their content library preferences to prioritize human-created designs over AI-generated ones.

🧩 How it works

To turn off generative AI features, users navigate to Profile > Settings > Permission and toggle off Enable generative AI features.

Separately, users can choose to see less AI-generated content by going to Profile > Your account > AI personalization and turning on the option to show less AI content. When this option is enabled, human-created content appears first when searching through Canva’s library for templates, graphics, and other design elements.

⚙️ Key details

  • Disabled Features: The toggle turns off many AI features, including:
    • Magic Write
    • Magic Design
    • Magic Layers
    • Magic Edit
    • Dream Lab
    • Canva Code
    • AI Shapes
    • Magic Expand (AI photo-extending)
    • Image generation via Canva chatbot
  • Enabled Features: Some AI-powered tools remain active because they “make everyday tasks faster without generating anything new.” These include:
    • Background remover
    • Magic Grab tool (lets you select an object in an image and move it somewhere else)
  • Content Library: Canva states that a “small portion” of its library consists of AI-generated content. Any design using these elements will have an AI label in its metadata.

💡 Why it matters

Since Canva’s significant push into AI in 2023, some users have expressed frustration with the influx of AI features and requested ways to disable them. Canva has continued to expand its AI-powered image-editing suite, including a prompt-powered editing update in April and the launch of its first in-house AI model, Canva Craft, last month. This new control allows users to manage their experience with these tools.

#Canva #GenerativeAI #DesignTools #UserControl

Source: Canva adds an AI ‘off’ button

item.title: Netflix adds AI Discover tab to TV app for themed content suggestions
item.description:
Netflix adds AI Discover tab to TV app for themed content suggestions

Netflix’s TV app is getting a new “AI Discover” tab where the company will show experimental, AI‑powered features to help you find new shows and movies to watch.

🔍 Overview

  • Netflix introduces an AI Discover tab in its TV app to surface experimental, AI‑powered recommendations.

🧩 How it works

  • The feature is powered by a new intelligence layer that “responds to what members tell us in real time and keeps learning.”
  • When you pick a theme, Netflix shows recommendations that match that theme.
  • If you don’t like a recommendation, you can tell Netflix, and the app will remember your feedback.

⚙️ Features

  • Themed recommendations such as “Something Light,” “Family Movie Night,” and “Quick Watches.”
  • Real‑time learning from user feedback.
  • Dedicated Discover tab in the top menu of the TV app.

🚀 Availability

  • The Discover tab appears along the top menu of the TV app.
  • Rolling out gradually in the United States.
  • Available to members who use Netflix in English on supported TVs.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a new way for members to discover content based on themes and personal feedback.
  • The announcement follows Netflix’s recent layoff of around 1,000 employees as growth has slowed and viewership has declined.

#Netflix #AI #Streaming #Recommendations

Source: Netflix will show you themed recommendations through a new ‘AI Discover’ tab

item.title: JavaScript Disabled Error Prevents Site Content Loading
item.description:
JavaScript Disabled Error Prevents Site Content Loading

A user attempting to access a web page encountered repeated messages indicating that JavaScript is disabled and that a required part of the site could not load.

🔍 Overview

  • “JavaScript is disabled in your browser.”
  • “Please enable JavaScript to proceed.”
  • “A required part of this site couldn’t load.”
  • “This may be due to a browser extension, network issues, or browser settings.”

⚙️ What happened

The same set of warnings appeared twice, confirming that the browser was not executing JavaScript and that essential site components failed to load.

🛠️ Suggested fixes

  • Enable JavaScript in the browser settings.
  • Check the internet connection.
  • Disable any ad‑blocking or privacy extensions.
  • Try accessing the site with a different browser.

These steps address the typical causes listed in the messages and can restore full site functionality.

#JavaScript #WebIssues #Browser

Source: Client Challenge
